constitutionalNote: Nobody writes the schema. The schema is a derivative, and derivatives are generated. A generated artifact holds no truth, defines no identity, and may not be edited by hand (UCL-C04, UCL-C05).

truthAsymmetry.metadata: canonical — registered, owned, versioned, certified, audited
truthAsymmetry.consequence: There is no such thing as 'the schema'. There are renderings, one per target space, all downstream of the same metadata.

lockInArgument: Lock-in is not a contract problem; it is a canonicity problem. A platform is locked into a database when the database holds the truth, because then the truth speaks that database's dialect. Here the truth lives in metadata; the database holds a derivative. Replacing the database is replacing a generator and regenerating. The same applies to API styles, message brokers, UI frameworks, cloud providers, and languages — each is a target space with a generator; none is canonical.
principles: GN-P1 every artifact is generated from registered, certified metadata
GN-P2 every generator is itself a registered, certified, replaceable artifact
GN-P3 generators preserve the six structural properties or are refused certification
GN-P4 reproducibility: same metadata + same generator version => identical artifact, bit-for-bit
GN-P5 hand-editing a generated artifact is a defect, detectable by the integrity checker
GN-P6 generation is policy-governed: who may request, for which targets, under which context
GN-P7 every generated artifact carries provenance: source metadata, generator identity, generator version, content attestation
GN-P8 multiple generators may target the same space; the choice is a deployment decision, never a property of the metadata

preservationRequirements.failure: rules exist in metadata but not in the artifact

preservationRequirements.standard: A generator preserving five of six is not mostly correct; it is uncertifiable, because the generated system would contradict its own description.

generators.writes: storage schemas in the registered dialect of a registered engine
generators.notes: Storage engine is a generator parameter. The ontology has never heard of SQL, and therefore SQL cannot constrain what the platform may express.

generators.writes: interface contracts in the registered style of a registered protocol
generators.notes: Protocol style (RPC / resource / graph / message) is a generator variant. The capability contract is canonical; the wire form is not.

generators.writes: event schemas, topic registrations, ordering guarantees
generators.notes: Temporal context is a required field (UCI-007) and a simulated event is structurally distinguishable from a real one — the generator refuses to omit the Reality dimension.

generators.writes: interface definitions in the registered framework's vocabulary
generators.notes: An unauthorised affordance is not rendered hidden — it is not generated at all. Hidden-but-present is the classic UI security defect. Locale is an input; a new language adds labels, not code.

generators.writes: constitutional documents, API references, data dictionaries, compliance packs, audit packs
generators.notes: Definitions are quoted verbatim — the generator may never paraphrase, because paraphrase is duplication (UCI-003). This document itself is a candidate for regeneration.

generators.writes: enforceable policy bundles in the registered enforcement engine's form
generators.notes: Precedence remains computed at evaluation, never flattened into an integer. Context conditions remain first-class, never compiled away.

generators.writes: executable workflow definitions for the registered runtime
generators.notes: Transition guards remain rule-evaluated, not inlined. Compensating actions are generated alongside their counterparts. The strictest-of-parts envelope (CM-P4) is enforced in the generated workflow.

generators.writes: graph projections: nodes, typed edges, ontological schemas
generators.notes: Every node is a registry entry; only registered relationship types appear; classification projects as edges, never as node properties. The knowledge graph cannot drift from the registries because it is generated from them.

generatorDAG: API Generator -> UI Generator (needs the generated contract surface)
Policy Generator -> Workflow Generator (needs enforceable rules)
Database Schema Generator -> Event Generator (needs projection shapes)
All -> Documentation Generator (needs every artifact's provenance)
Circular generator dependency is a cycle and is refused (UCI-014).
stalePropagation: When source metadata changes, the artifact becomes STALE and regeneration is requested by policy — automatic or approval-gated. Without this, metadata and artifacts drift apart within a week. A deployment that refuses to regenerate is a visible, governed decision rather than an invisible decay.

lifecycle.note: Certification requires a preservation proof and a test vector suite: known metadata => expected artifact. Retired artifacts leave deployment but their provenance records are permanent (UCI-011).

security: GN-S-01 a generator may only read registries within its certified scope
GN-S-02 attestations are issued by the Certification pipeline, not by the generator — it cannot forge its own provenance (GI-1, GI-4)
GN-S-03 secrets come from the deployment contract, never embedded in metadata or generated artifacts
GN-S-04 unauthorised affordances are absent at generation, not hidden at runtime
GN-S-05 integrity checking detects hand-edits; a hand-edited artifact is non-compliant
GN-S-06 a simulated reality context propagates visibly into every generated artifact
answeringTheObjection: It is often false. Hand-built schemas drift from intent precisely because nothing forces them to follow it. A generated schema is guaranteed to match its metadata; a hand-built one is guaranteed nothing.

Where it is true, the deficiency is in the metadata, not in the generation. Fixing the metadata improves every artifact at once — schema, API, UI, docs, policies, graph — which is strictly better than fixing one artifact and leaving five to drift.

Nothing here forbids hand-crafted artifacts. It forbids hand-edited generated artifacts. A bespoke artifact is a new registered capability or a new generator, admitted through the constitution with a preservation proof. The constraint is not 'no craft'; it is 'no unregistered truth'.
